summary: Jae-gwon Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Ryukoku University by 2007 and later held a post there.
Jagaddhar Zadoo was an Indologist who worked at the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir, where his posts are attested from 1924 to 1930 and as Superintendent in 1947.

Jagadish Chandra Chatterji (b. 1875) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who earned a B.A. at the University of Cambridge. In 1911, he is attested as Director of the Research and Archaeological Department in Jammu and Kashmir.

Jagannath Upadhyaya was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He was a professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1980–1983) and in 1985 became the first director of the Rare Buddhist Text Research Project at CIHTS.

Jagdish Kashyap (1908–1976), a Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics scholar, studied at Patna College, BHU, and under Rahul Sankrityayan. He taught at BHU (~1940–1951), Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1959–1965), and directed Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1951–1973).

Jaideva Singh (1893–1986) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, studying under Swami Lakshman Joo, Srikrishna Harihirlekar, and Nankoo Bhaya Telang. He was chief producer at All India Radio (~1956–1962) and chairman of Uttar Pradesh Sangeet Natak Akademi (1973).

Jake H. Davis, a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies, earned an MA at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a PhD at the CUNY Graduate Center. He held posts at Brown University, CCNY, and New York University.

Jakob Steiner (1796–1863) studied at Heidelberg University (1818–1821) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1822–1824). He held posts at the University of Applied Sciences Berlin (1825–1834) and Frederick William University Berlin (1834–1863).

Jakob Wilhelm Hauer (1881–1962), a scholar of Indology and religious studies, studied at Oxford and under Richard von Garbe at Tübingen. He served as professor at the University of Marburg (1925–1927) and held a chair at Tübingen (1927–1945).

James A. Benn works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, SOAS, and UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr., and held faculty posts at Lewis & Clark College, Arizona State University, and McMaster University.

James A. Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He served as Professor of Religion at California State University (attested 1998) and as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).
James Adam (1860–1907) was a philosopher who completed his studies at the University of Aberdeen (~1876–1880) and Gonville and Caius College (~1880–1884).

James Alan Matisoff (b. 1937) is a linguist, Sinologist, and Tibetologist educated at Harvard, International Christian University, and UC Berkeley. He taught at Columbia University (1966–1969) before serving at the University of California, Berkeley from 1970 to 2002.

James Atkinson (1780–1852), a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology, studied at the University of Edinburgh. He held positions at the India Government Mint in Kolkata and was Assistant Persian Professor at Fort William College in 1818.
James B. Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under John D. Dunne, receiving his PhD in 1996.

James Blumenthal (1967–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He held faculty posts at Oregon State University and Maitripa College.

James Burgess (1832–1916) was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Glasgow and Edinburgh. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India, including as Director General (1886–1889), and was Vice President of the Royal Society of Edinburgh (1908–1914).

James Burnell Robinson (b. 1944) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Richard Hugh Robinson and Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He was Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa (~1975–2012).

James C. Dobbins specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Yale University by 1984 and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland (1792–1844) was an Indologist who studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck. He served as a professor of law at Presidency University.
